features.evidence: whre, thhat, habit trcker
features.name: Proofreading care
features.description: Captures how carefully the letter is edited at the surface level, including spelling, grammar, and sentence integrity.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors distract from the message or make passages feel careless.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the overall meaning remains clear.
Only minor mistakes appear; the prose still feels mostly polished.
The letter reads as clean and well edited throughout.

features.evidence: I started my career on the unglamorous side of software
features.name: Narrative framing
features.description: Captures whether the letter gives the reader a coherent story or distinctive point of view rather than a checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Mostly a generic application note or list of claims with little unifying thread.
Shows a theme or hook, but it fades into resume restatement.
Presents a clear throughline linking background, motivation, and fit.
Uses memorable framing that makes the applicant's path and value easy to remember.

features.evidence: foundational infrastructure is where I choose to work
features.name: Foundational leverage orientation
features.description: Captures how strongly the writer is motivated by improving central systems whose benefits propagate across many teams.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of interest in platform or foundation work.
Expresses general excitement about scale or impact.
Shows a clear preference for foundational work whose benefits spread across teams.
Makes a well reasoned case for seeking inherited leverage at company scale.

features.evidence: make the secure path the easy path for busy product engineers
features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant frames security work as helping developers succeed through usable defaults and lower-friction tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not show much concern for developer usability or downstream adoption.
Mentions helping other teams, but only in broad terms.
Clearly emphasizes reducing friction or making secure behavior easier.
Shows repeated empathy for downstream developers and treats usability as central to security impact.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: Security automation vision
features.description: Captures whether the letter understands the role as scaling scarce security judgment through automation rather than just writing backend code.

levels.descriptor: No real framing of security automation as a core problem.
Mentions automation as a task or convenience.
Describes automation as a way to expand security capacity or reduce toil.
Shows a sophisticated view of scaling judgment through triage, variant analysis, or expert-multiplying systems.

features.evidence: variant analysis
features.name: Responsibility mapping
features.description: Captures how directly the letter ties the applicant's background to this team's specific responsibilities instead of only to generic security engineering.

levels.descriptor: Describes fit in general terms only.
Connects background to one posted responsibility.
Connects several experiences to the responsibilities named in the posting.
Maps background tightly to the team's stated charter, workflow, and technical stack.

features.evidence: 3 years ... 5 years ... 7 years
features.name: Experience tenure
features.description: Captures the depth of professional software experience explicitly claimed in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Claims roughly 2 to 3 years of relevant professional experience.
Claims roughly 4 to 5 years of relevant professional experience.
Claims 6 or more years of relevant professional experience.

features.evidence: launching 2 production services ... launching 6 production services
features.name: Launch record
features.description: Captures how much direct evidence the letter gives of having shipped and maintained multiple production services.

levels.descriptor: Claims launch experience on 1 to 2 production services.
Claims launch experience on 3 to 4 production services.
Claims launch experience on 5 or more production services.

features.evidence: Go as the language I have used most
features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how convincingly the letter establishes Go as a primary production language for relevant backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is merely listed or mentioned in passing.
Go is named as a main language, but without role-shaped examples.
Go is presented as a primary production language for backend or systems work.
Shows strong Go ownership tied directly to relevant systems such as backends, guardrails, or operated services.

features.evidence: Python became my workhorse
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how much substantive Python experience the letter shows, especially in automation, tooling, or services.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only named briefly.
Python is mentioned as a tool the applicant uses.
Shows substantial Python use in production tooling, services, or automation.
Shows deep Python ownership across multiple relevant uses such as agents, analysis, automation, and internal services.

features.evidence: comfortable across 9 other languages
features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of other programming languages the letter claims beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.evidence: Bachelor's degree ... Master's degree ... Doctoral degree
features.name: Educational attainment
features.description: Captures the highest degree level explicitly claimed in the letter, which is relevant because advanced study is preferred in the posting.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent level only.
Master's degree.
Doctoral degree.

features.evidence: Python agents that plan and execute bounded tasks, supervised by Go services that log and constrain every step
features.name: Agentic architecture experience
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows real design experience with agent systems, especially around bounded actions, permissions, auditability, or guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful agent-system experience is shown.
Mentions agentic tooling, but without architectural detail.
Describes a clear agent architecture, often with a Go and Python split.
Shows mature agent-system design with explicit autonomy boundaries, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.evidence: shipping LLM-backed features and hardening them against unpredictable inputs
features.name: AI deployment maturity
features.description: Captures the depth of practical AI experience, especially whether the writer has operated model-backed features with evaluation or reliability concerns in mind.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is shown.
Mentions AI or LLM work in broad terms only.
Shows production experience shipping model-backed features.
Shows production AI experience plus evaluation, hardening, trust, or failure-mode awareness.

features.evidence: automated vulnerability report handling
features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has already automated intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-triage automation experience is shown.
Mentions automation around vulnerability handling, but vaguely.
Gives a clear example of triage automation such as classification, routing, or deduplication.
Shows a strong triage system with concrete workflow change, scale effect, or a largely self-serve pipeline.

features.evidence: performed security assessments across the stack
features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures the degree of hands-on experience performing structured security reviews rather than only building general software.

levels.descriptor: No real security assessment experience is shown.
Mentions security review in generic or limited terms.
Shows clear assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or validation of fixes.
Shows repeated or cross-stack assessment practice with a clear method or engineering mindset.

features.evidence: turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation
features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides convincing evidence of data-structure or algorithm skill beyond a bare claim.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful algorithmic evidence is shown.
Claims fluency, but offers little concrete support.
Provides one concrete example of an algorithmic or data-structure redesign.
Provides a strong recent example showing clear structural or performance improvement from algorithmic choices.

features.evidence: most recently collapsing a tangle of lookups into one well-chosen structure
features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how often the letter backs claims with concrete examples, named systems, or recent technical wins.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on abstract claims or adjective-heavy assertions.
Includes some concrete details, but many claims remain generic.
Uses several specific examples that make major claims easier to trust.
Repeatedly grounds claims in concrete, recent, technically intelligible examples.

features.evidence: the queue went from a dreaded chore to something the tooling mostly runs itself
features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter states the outcome of the applicant's work, not just the fact that they did it.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists duties or technologies with little sense of outcome.
Implies positive effect, but without a clear result.
States a clear before-and-after outcome for at least one contribution.
Shows vivid or quantified operational impact that explains what changed for the team.

features.evidence: someone always inherits what we build
features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, failure modes, and durable systems behavior rather than feature shipping alone.

levels.descriptor: Shows little attention to maintainability or resilience.
Uses generic reliability language without much depth.
Shows a clear maintainer or resilience-oriented framing.
Backs a reliability mindset with concrete attention to failure cases, inherited systems, or stewardship.

features.evidence: replicated log store with failover from first principles
features.name: Project rigor
features.description: Captures how technically ambitious the applicant's personal or side projects appear, especially when they tackle distributed systems or hard guarantees.

levels.descriptor: No outside project is mentioned, or the example is trivial.
Mentions a small useful side project with limited technical depth.
Shows a meaningful system project with substantive engineering choices.
Shows an ambitious project that confronts hard guarantees, distributed coordination, or failure recovery.

features.evidence: regularly send patches upstream
features.name: Open source patching
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows a habit of fixing upstream dependencies rather than only consuming them.

levels.descriptor: No upstream fixing behavior is shown.
Mentions occasional or general patch submission.
Shows a recurring habit of diagnosing defects and sending corrective patches upstream.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source project with a genuine user community
features.name: Open source maintenance
features.description: Captures the depth of ongoing responsibility for a public project, such as reviews, releases, roadmap, or community support.

levels.descriptor: No public project stewardship is shown.
Mentions a public project, but without much maintenance responsibility.
Shows ownership of maintaining a public project or library.
Shows stewardship of an actively used project with releases, reviews, and external users or contributors.

features.evidence: capture-the-flag competitions
features.name: Offensive practice
features.description: Captures whether the letter shows ongoing adversarial practice through CTFs or a clearly articulated attacker mindset.

levels.descriptor: No offensive practice or attacker-oriented evidence is shown.
Mentions CTFs or attacker thinking lightly or occasionally.
Shows regular CTF participation or sustained offensive practice.
Shows serious commitment through strong placements or clearly high-level competitive practice.

features.evidence: OSCP certification
features.name: Security certification
features.description: Captures external security validation claimed in the letter, with stronger credit for hands-on certifications.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
Shows a baseline certification such as Security+.
Shows a hands-on certification such as OSCP.
